headlines.article_text: Bank of America (BAC) Q3 2026 earnings Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu In this article BAC Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Brian Moynihan, Chairman and CEO of Bank of America, speaks with Economic Club of Washington Chair David Rubenstein at an event at the Ritz-Carlton on February 25, 2025 in Washington, DC. Anna Moneymaker | Getty Images Bank of America posted a sharp profit decline after being hit with a $1.2 billion penalty by U.S. regulators, while revenue also disappointed after trading operations generated about $750 million less than expected. Shares of the bank fell more than 4% in premarket trading. Here's what the company reported: Earnings per share: 91 cents, may not compare with $1.10 LSEG estimate Revenue: $30.12 billion vs. $30.69 billion estimate The bank's third-quarter profit fell 17% to $6.93 billion, or 91 cents a share. Excluding the penalty, which sapped income by 17 cents, EPS would've been $1.08 a share. Companywide revenue rose 3.2% to $30.12 billion in the quarter, but that was below expectations by about $570 million, largely on misses from Wall Street trading operations. Fixed income trading revenue fell 17% to $2.55 billion on weakness in mortgages, municipals, and credit activity. That is roughly $450 million below the StreetAccount estimate. Equities trading revenue climbed 10% to $2.51 billion, but that was also below analysts' expectations, by nearly $300 million. Investment banking revenue dropped 11% to $1.8 billion, roughly in line with expectations. Net interest income, a key profitability driver watched closely by Bank of America investors, rose 7.9% to $16.6 billion, slightly edging out the $16.53 estimate. The Treasury episode, in which U.S. regulators said the company failed to report billions of dollars in suspicious transactions, will inevitably spark questions as to whether CEO Brian Moynihan has a handle on controls at the second-biggest U.S. bank by assets. Moynihan took the helm in 2010 and spent the early years of his tenure making amends for mortgage-related abuses in the aftermath of the 2008 financial crisis. Now, questions arise as to whether there are any more risk-management issues waiting to be found. The Treasury announcement adds 11th-hour intrigue to what was an otherwise fairly routine bank earnings week. On Tuesday, JPMorgan Chase, Goldman Sachs, Citigroup and Wells Fargo posted mixed results, with JPMorgan missing EPS and revenue estimates for the first time in years. This story is developing. headlines.title: BlackRock draws $205 billion in client funds as quarterly profit beats estimates
headlines.summary: BlackRock's assets under management — which determine a large chunk of its earnings — rose to $15.49 trillion, from $13.46 trillion a year earlier.
headlines.article_text: BlackRock draws $205 billion in client funds as quarterly profit beats estimates Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu In this article BLK Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT The BlackRock logo is pictured outside the company's headquarters in the Manhattan borough of New York City on May 25, 2021. Carlo Allegri | Reuters BlackRock surpassed Wall Street profit expectations and attracted $205 billion in total inflows in the third quarter, sending the world's largest asset manager's shares up 5% in premarket trading on ⁠Wednesday. The benchmark S&P 500 extended its steady climb in the quarter to hover near its all-time highs on a rally in AI-focused ​stocks, encouraging investors to pour ​money into asset management firms ​such as BlackRock. "Market fundamentals are strong and well supported, with higher margins and earnings momentum catalyzed by new technology," CEO Larry Fink said in a statement. BlackRock's assets under management — which determine a large chunk of the earnings — ⁠rose ‌to $15.49 trillion, from $13.46 trillion a year earlier and $15.34 trillion ⁠in the second quarter. The growth was driven by a combination of $134.5 billion of new flows into BlackRock's flagship iShares ETFs, and the rising valuations of its investments in a robust equity market. The company posted an adjusted profit of $15.93 per share, beating Wall Street ‌expectations of $14.13, according to data compiled by LSEG. The robust results will help alleviate pressure on BlackRock's shares, which have underperformed the broader market this year over fears of a slowdown in ​activity from cautious investor sentiment. Even as markets have remained sturdy, the combination of surging bond yields and the expectation that the Federal Reserve's recent interest rate hike marks the beginning of a tightening cycle has called into question whether the rally can be sustained. Higher yields over a ⁠sustained period can put pressure on markets as investors rotate capital into safe-haven assets, locking in better risk-adjusted returns. Net flows into ‌BlackRock's debt products were $78.2 billion in the quarter, signaling strong investor ‌appetite despite the recent steep selloff in Treasuries. Redemptions ease in private credit BlackRock has accelerated its push into private credit markets in recent years. The asset class typically generates higher fees than the firm's main source of profits, its suite ⁠of ETFs, which depends on high volumes of inflows to boost earnings. The company has spelled out plans ⁠to deliver more than $35 billion in revenue by the end of the decade, with ⁠over 30% of that coming from private markets and technology. The private credit industry has come under scrutiny from investors concerned about lenders' exposure to software companies seen as particularly ​vulnerable to disruption from AI, as well as the ‌opacity of valuations. Those concerns prompted a surge in redemption requests from investors in recent quarters. That pressure, however, seems to be easing, with most large managers of private credit funds reporting slowing redemption requests in the third quarter. BlackRock's HPS Corporate Lending Fund saw redemption requests fall to roughly 11.5% of shares in the latest quarter, from 13.3% in ​the second quarter. While BlackRock does not break ‌out its revenue from private markets, net flows in this category were $15.31 billion in the quarter. headlines.article_text: Stocks making the biggest moves premarket: BAC, BLK, HPE Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Check out the companies making the biggest moves premarket: Bank of America — The stock tumbled 4% after the company reported a sharp decline in third-quarter profit due to a $1.2 billion penalty from the U.S. Treasury Department over money-laundering violations. Profit fell 17% to 91 cents per share, but that would have been $1.08 per share without the penalty. BlackRock — The asset manager rose 3% after it reported an earnings and revenue beat . Adjusted earnings came in at $15.93 per share, compared with the $14.13 per share expected by analysts polled by LSEG. Assets under management rose to $15.49 trillion, up from $13.46 trillion one year ago. ASML — U.S.-listed shares of the Dutch semiconductor company fell 1% after the company reported a slight miss on net sales in its third-quarter financial report. Those came in at 11.66 billion euros, compared to analysts polled by LSEG's estimate of 11.72 billion euros. However, net profit came in above expectations. GameStop — Shares gained 2% after GameStop CEO and Chairman Ryan Cohen disclosed in a regulatory filing that he bought 844,000 shares. Albemarle — The chemical manufacturing company jumped 3% after Mizuho upgraded the stock to outperform from neutral. Mizuho analysts said that demand for lithium is exceeding expectations, which they said Albemarle with its improved balance sheet can capitalize on. Dell Technologies , Hewlett Packard Enterprise — Shares were down more than 2.5% and nearly 4%, respectively, after Barclays downgraded the stocks to equal weight from overweight. Both stocks have rallied in 2026, with Dell up more than 350% and HPE rising 185%, but analysts at the bank are doubtful these rallies can be sustained much longer. Morgan Stanley — Shares were slightly higher by 0.4% after the company reported an earnings and revenue beat in its third-quarter financial report. Equity revenues came in above expectations, while revenues from its investment banking arm missed estimates. — CNBC's Sarah Min contributed reporting
